look_here_first: Look at bark and leaf texture together: Chinese elm has distinctive exfoliating mottled tan/orange/gray bark and small glossy, mostly singly serrate leaves; it flowers and fruits in late summer-fall.

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: introduced Asian elm, often planted and sometimes naturalized

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: mature bark exfoliates in irregular plates creating mottled tan, orange, gray and olive patches

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: leaves small, dark, lustrous/glabrous above, mostly singly serrate

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: flowers in late summer to early fall

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: small glabrous samara; seed nearly fills samara

key_traits.label: Identification
key_traits.text: disturbed-site escape/naturalization makes it a useful field comparison

key_traits.label: Elm training
key_traits.text: Read leaf texture/asymmetry together with twig wings, bark, reproductive season and samara characters.
